item.description: Gov. Mike Dunleavy said lawmakers are mistaken if they think things will be easier under a new governor next year.

item.title: Juneau Assembly to vote on $2.3M worth of affordable housing funding
item.description: The projects proposed this year would help create more than 40 units of housing, comprising both single-family homes and apartment complexes, all across the borough.

item.title: Community testifies in support of TCLL staff, union contracts at Juneau School Board forum
item.description: Support for grant funded positions and teacher’s contracts became the main issue during the Juneau School Board’s budget public forum last week.

item.title: Murkowski tries to reassure Greenlanders still shaken by Trump’s threats
item.description: President Trump ruled out taking Greenland by force, but what if he changes his mind? Murkowski says Congress would stop him, even if her GOP colleagues won't say so now.

item.title: One phone call at a time, Kipnuk residents vote on whether to rebuild or relocate
item.description: Kipnuk leaders are calling hundreds of tribal members to determine the village's future after last fall's storm caused widespread destruction.

item.title: Facing opposition, Dunleavy says lawmakers should ‘take more time’ on his tax bill
item.description: Gov. Mike Dunleavy's sales tax proposal faces sharp opposition. Now, he says he's open to putting the tax bill on ice — but asking lawmakers pass the rest of his fiscal plan.

item.title: Juneau musicians welcome ruling granting breweries unlimited live music
item.description: Until last month, breweries were limited to hosting four live shows a year. Before 2024, they were banned from having them completely.

item.title: Juneau Assembly OKs more than $2M toward affordable housing projects
item.description: The projects approved Monday are expected to create more than 40 housing units, including both single-family homes and apartment complexes located throughout the borough.
